where.screen_path: /login (Fresh signed-out → FreshOnboarding 6-step state machine), / (onboarding-setup overlay → unlocked HomeScreen with founding identity + first entry)

what.summary: Shipped Fresh roadmap Cut 5: the 90-second compose-before-login state machine. Volatile bundle (text + attachment + display name + passphrase) held in module-level memory across the FreshOnboarding-to-WalletProvider unmount-remount handoff; never localStorage, never sessionStorage, never IndexedDB. WalletProvider gained an onboarding-setup phase that consumes the bundle and runs createWallet + identity attestation + first journal entry under a Fresh-styled overlay, then lands in unlocked. LoginPage now lazy-loads FreshLoginShell so Classic operators pay zero Fresh bytes; login bundle dropped from 14.15KB gz to 11.09KB. One commit, four gates green.

why.text: Cut 5 of the 2026-05-24 Fresh young-adult-friendly theme + IA roadmap, deferred by the prior session as a dedicated-session piece because it inverts the existing auth-then-wallet ceremony. The compose-first inversion is the brief's central UX move: the first signed entry exists in the wallet by the time login completes. The operator never sees a PassphrasePrompt or an IdentityCeremony during Fresh onboarding because they have already answered every question those screens ask.

outcome.notes: [P-CUT-5] ✓ Compose-before-login 90-second state machine (commit 46cb505). FreshOnboarding.tsx implements splash → compose → name → passphrase → recovery primer → email → OTP code. Volatile bundle in src/features/onboarding/pendingOnboarding.ts (module-level memory only — passphrase never persisted). applyOnboardingBundle.ts signs founding identity + first journal entry post-sign-in. WalletProvider's new onboarding-setup phase guards via ranRef against StrictMode double-invoke. LoginPage React.lazy of FreshLoginShell drops login bundle 14.15KB → 11.09KB gz so Classic operators pay zero Fresh bytes. Bundle budgets: WalletProvider bumped 7.5KB → 8KB to absorb new phase; new FreshLoginShell lazy chunk budgeted at 5.5KB (current 4.19KB). One file-size warning (FreshOnboarding.tsx 751 lines, under 800 hard limit). All four gates green: typecheck ✓ / lint ✓ / 48 tests ✓ / build ✓. Keys-never-leave audit: no new code path logs, persists, or transmits a key, seed, or passphrase. [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: brief was tight enough that Cut 5 landed in one session; the prior carpenter's recommendation to treat 5/6/7 as dedicated sessions was correct.

next: Operator browser-verifies the Cut 5 flow against Netlify+Supabase: pick Fresh in Settings → Appearance, sign out, walk /login through the 90s onboarding, confirm /  lands with founding identity + first entry already signed. Then choose Cut 6 (Sage persona activation, voice-dependent on operator authorship) or Cut 7 (share cards + Quick-share presets, design-heavier, less voice-dependent) as the next dispatch. My read: Cut 7 lands more independent audience-facing value sooner because share cards are the audience's distribution channel.
